bond_pricer_floating_rate.text:
`zero_coupon_bond_pricer` answers "what is a bond with a single payment at maturity worth today at one flat yield?" You give it `face_value`, `yield_rate`, `maturity` and optionally `frequency` (default 2), and it discounts the redemption value back using `face / (1 + y/m)^(m·T)`.

`bond_pricer_floating_rate` answers "what is a floating-rate note worth, given projected forward rates?" It prices a stream of coupons, each set from a `reference_rates` entry plus a `spread`, and discounts each cashflow with its own per-period `discount_rates` value, with `face_value` repaid at the end.

So the first has no coupons and one yield, while the second has rate-driven coupons and a discount curve. The floating-rate pricer also takes the number of periods from the length of `reference_rates`, and `maturity` must agree with it. Its default `frequency` is 4, versus 2 for the zero-coupon pricer.

explain.text: The Zero Coupon Bond Pricer (`zero_coupon_bond_pricer`) prices a zero-coupon bond by discounting its single redemption payment back to today. It uses the formula face value divided by (1 + y/m) raised to the power m·T, where y is the annual yield, m the compounding frequency and T the years to maturity. You supply `face_value`, `yield_rate` (as a decimal) and `maturity` in years, and optionally `frequency`, which defaults to 2 compounding periods per year. pyvar does the calculation and returns the bond's price.

when.text:
The Zero Coupon Bond Pricer (`zero_coupon_bond_pricer`) fits when you need the present value of a single payment at maturity:

- You hold or are analysing a bond that pays only its `face_value` at maturity, with no coupons along the way.
- You have an annual yield (`yield_rate`, as a decimal) and a time to maturity in years (`maturity`), and want the price that follows from them.
- You need to match a particular compounding convention: set `frequency` to the number of compounding periods per year (it defaults to 2).
- You want a simple discounting building block, since the price is just the face value discounted at the given yield.

If your bond does pay coupons, `bond_pricer_fixed_coupon` is listed as pricing a fixed-coupon bond by discounting its cashflows at a flat yield.
